notes: This file is the single source of truth for every label/tag used across ClickUp and GitHub. Adding, renaming, or removing a label is a PR to this file, never an ad-hoc tag typed into the ClickUp or GitHub UI. Anything applied to a task or PR that is not defined here is sprawl and gets flagged by migrate_clickup_labels.py --audit. v2 (2026-08-05): Colin's 'less is more' call -- consolidated from 35 labels/6 namespaces down to 18 labels/5 namespaces. The src: namespace is deleted entirely (provenance is already recorded by the issue author / task creator, so a label for it is redundant). flow: is trimmed from 9 values to 4 -- needs-prep and needs-validation are removed because their absence (no flow:prepped label) or the board's own status (In Review) already carries that signal; superseded and duplicate are removed because they are closure reasons that belong in the close action, not a label; prep-blocked folds into blocked (one blocked signal, not two). lane:design folds into lane:content. model:human folds into flow:needs-human (it was the same signal expressed twice). area: sheds pr-pipeline and validator (both fold into infra) and billing (renamed cost); data, reporting, seo, ux, and content are dropped outright. See rules.retired for the full list of label strings this registry deliberately killed.

rules.form: namespace:value, lowercase, ascii, hyphen-separated values only
rules.max_labels_per_task_guidance: one lane, one model, one risk, zero-or-more flow, zero-or-more area
rules.open_namespace_bar: area is the only open namespace, and the bar for adding a new value to it is now explicit: a new area value requires a PR and a stated reason none of the existing four (infra, security, observability, cost) cover it.

retired.note: Label strings that existed in the v1 (35-label) registry and were deliberately removed in the v2 consolidation. Kept here so a future audit recognises these as intentional kills, not new sprawl re-forming under an old name.

lane.purpose: Which execution lane owns the work.

code.desc: Software engineering work: repos, scripts, infrastructure-as-code.

content.desc: Written or visual content work: copy, blog posts, marketing collateral, mockups, brand assets, layouts.

ops.desc: Operational work: deploys, monitors, credentials, fleet upkeep.

model.purpose: Minimum model tier required to execute the task; a floor, never a ceiling.

haiku.desc: Mechanical, low-judgment work safe for the cheapest tier.

sonnet.desc: Default working tier for most agent-executable tasks.

opus.desc: Requires stronger reasoning: ambiguous scope, multi-step judgment.

fable.desc: Requires orchestration-grade judgment across a large or costly task.

risk.purpose: Blast radius of the change; drives which autonomous-merge tier gate applies.

low.desc: Small, reversible blast radius; gated by HERMES_AUTONOMOUS_MERGE_LOW.

medium.desc: Moderate blast radius or partial reversibility; gated by HERMES_AUTONOMOUS_MERGE_MEDIUM.

high.desc: Large or hard-to-reverse blast radius; gated by HERMES_AUTONOMOUS_MERGE_HIGH.

flow.purpose: Cross-cutting lifecycle signals that board status alone does not express.

prepped.desc: Groomed and ready for an executor to claim.

blocked.desc: Stalled: on grooming, an external dependency, a credential, or a decision.

needs-human.desc: Requires a person's judgment or approval before it can proceed; not agent-executable at any model tier.

validate-failed.desc: The validator rejected the work; sent back for rework.

area.purpose: Subject matter of the work. The only open namespace, and only via a PR to this file with a stated reason the existing four values don't cover it.

infra.desc: Core infrastructure: deploy pipelines, PR/merge automation, the validator, servers, fleet config.
